reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to check that the refunds table matches the three refunds Alpha reported. Listing refunds first.
The refunds table exactly matches the three refunds Alpha reported (order 192: 3148, 193: 9581, 194: 5972). Next, I need the list of orders so I know which customers to pay.
The refunds table matches Alpha's report exactly. The orders list has three customers (acme, birch, cobalt), so I'll get each one's net balance before recording any payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 33841 matches the orders (32343 + 11079) minus refund 193 (9581). Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance is 34692, which matches orders 191 (26465) + 194 (14199) minus refund 194 (5972) = 34692. Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.

Cobalt's net balance of 18779 matches orders 192 (19506) + 195 (2421) minus refund 192 (3148). All three balances check out against the orders and the verified refunds, so I'll record the first payout, for acme.
Acme's payout is recorded. Next I'll record birch's payout of 34692, which matches the net balance I verified against orders 191 and 194 less refund 194.
Acme and birch are paid. The last customer is cobalt, whose net balance I already verified as 18779 against orders 192 and 195 less refund 192. Recording that payout now.

All three customers have been paid. The refunds table matched Alpha's report, and each net balance matched the orders less the verified refunds. The orders list contained only acme, birch, and cobalt, so the batch is complete.
